chunks.subject: AP Environmental Science
chunks.title: Q1 Design an Investigation (10 points) — Set 1: chickadees, spiders & nonnative plants
chunks.content: AP Environmental Science FRQ 1 is 'Design an Investigation,' 10 points, one point per lettered part (A–H, some split into i/ii; 10 scored points total). The task mixes identify/describe/explain skills with reading data from figures and reasoning about an investigation's design (scientific question, variables). Set 1 answer key: A [P1] a K-selected reproductive strategy (few offspring, high parental care, late maturity, reproduce multiple times). B [P2] a decrease in spiders raises insects (prey released) and lowers plants. C [P3] read the figure: ~2 spiders per sample at 25% nonnative plants. D [P4] trend: as nonnative-plant % increases, insects decrease (inverse relationship). E [P5] Figure 2 support: below 25% the chickadee growth rate is at/above replacement (positive). F(i) [P6] a valid scientific question (does mowing affect ant species richness?); F(ii) [P7] dependent variable = number of ant species. G(i) [P8] the more diverse unmowed grassland recovers better (redundancy/adaptation). G(ii) [P9] a paved playground would show fewer species (unsuitable habitat). H [P10] an effect of a paved road on animals (roadkill, fragmentation/isolation, noise). Common failure: describing r-selected traits for A; naming the independent variable or a non-measurable variable for the dependent variable (F ii); vague 'more diverse' for G(i) without the redundancy/adaptation mechanism.

chunks.subject: AP Environmental Science
chunks.title: Q1 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 1A, 10/10
chunks.content: Q1 (Set 1) scored 10/10 (all parts A–H). K-selected 'few offspring' cared for longer (A); spider decrease → insect increase (B); ~2 spiders at 25% (C); insects decrease as nonnative % rises (D); growth rate above replacement below 25% (E); mowing/ant-diversity question and 'number of ant species' dependent variable (F); higher grassland gene pool → survivable genotypes more likely, plus niche partitioning (G i); paved playground fewer species from lack of primary producers (G ii); paved road inhibits migration (H). Full-credit model.

chunks.subject: AP Environmental Science
chunks.title: Q1 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 1B, 6/10
chunks.content: Q1 (Set 1) scored 6/10. Earned C (2 spiders), D (insects decrease as nonnative % rises), E (growth rate above replacement below 25%), F(i) (mowed-vs-unmowed biodiversity question), F(ii) (amount of ant species), and H (road barrier impedes crossing). Lost A (described r-selected traits — 'many offspring, short lifespan'), B (said both plants AND insects increase, mixing trophic effects), and both G points (G i only said 'greater biodiversity' without the recovery mechanism; G ii compared to the urban park's disturbance rather than habitat suitability). Illustrates that data-reading and identification points are earned while the explanation points (A, B, G) are missed.

chunks.subject: AP Environmental Science
chunks.title: Q1 Set 1 exemplar — Sample 1C, 3/10
chunks.content: Q1 (Set 1) scored 3/10. Earned only C (2 spiders at 25%), D (higher nonnative % → fewer insects), and H (road barrier cuts off resources). Lost A (vague 'build nests and lay eggs,' not a K-selected strategy), B (said lower trophic levels increase, missing the plant decrease), E (growth rate 'at 0' does not show it is at/above replacement below 25%), F(i)/F(ii) (question and dependent variable not valid — named a mowing condition, an independent variable), and both G points. Illustrates a low response holding only two figure-reading points and the road effect.
